name: @w6w-apps/placid
description: Generate images, PDFs and videos from Placid templates, and manage templates, collections, fonts and uploaded media.

w6w.longDescription:
Placid is a creative-automation service: you design a template in its editor, name the layers you want to change, and the REST API (v2.0) renders a finished image, PDF or video from your data. This app covers the documented REST surface: create, retrieve and delete images, PDFs (including merging existing PDFs by URL) and videos; list, create, retrieve, update and delete templates; manage template collections; manage custom fonts; and upload media to Placid storage for use in picture layers.

Every render is asynchronous. A create call answers with a queued record carrying a `polling_url`; poll the matching Retrieve action, or pass a `webhook_success` URL and Placid will POST the finished record. Layer content is passed as one JSON object keyed by the layer names from the template (`{"title": {"text": "Hello"}}`), exactly as the API takes it.

Health is reported from what the API exposes. Placid has no whoami or account endpoint, so the credential probe is a cheap template-list read, an unsigned reachability check treats the API's own `{"message":"Unauthenticated."}` 401 as proof the API is serving, and a quota check reads the documented `X-RateLimit-*` headers (60 requests per minute). Placid's status page (status.placid.app) is real but client-rendered with no JSON, RSS or Atom feed, so vendor status is declared unavailable rather than faked.
